$comment: A CALL BEFORE ANY DECLARATION OF ITS CALLEE DECLARES IT IMPLICITLY, AND THE LATER DEFINITION IS THE FUNCTION CALLED (C90 6.3.2.2; P69 round 1, lane cs, fold f26c, D-C-A-CALL-BEFORE-ANY-DECLARATION-MAKES-NO-IMPLICIT-DECLARATION). MEASURED by lane cs's probes ip and ip3 (each built and RUN): `int b(void) { return f(40) + 2; } int f(int v) { return v; }` runs 42 on gcc 13.3.0 (default and -std=c2x), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and cl 19.51, each warning the implicit declaration; clang 18.1.3 refuses it. One working reference makes it required. Before this fold DSS bound the call to the later definition IN SILENCE, through an order-blind lookup that also read a later object's value (the first item of this fold). Every return before 42 names the first fact that failed. The release arm pins that the optimizer keeps both calls the definition's.
$expectWarningsComment: ONE warning for two calls of one name, at the first (line 1, the callee `f`).
